title: sample-splicing-batcher-and-econ-adapter-for-bursty-traffic
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: production traffic at several customers shows bursty, highly-skewed arrival patterns where opportunistic batching and static prefill rules under-utilize GPUs during microbursts while aggressive batching harms tail latency. This PR introduces two coordinated features: (1) a sample-splicing micro-batcher that slices incoming requests into short adaptive windows and dynamically stitches small samples into micro-batches with low-overhead aggregation, and (2) an econ-adapter that computes per-segment unit-economics and toggles conservative quantization + prefill/kv-cache policies when cost regressions are detected. This work targets cost optimization automation for bursty workloads without sacrificing 99.9th percentile latency SLOs. Summary of changes: added a new micro-batching runtime module (batcher/sample_splice.go and associated tests), an econ-adapter controller (control/econ_adapter.go) that subscribes to route telemetry and applies policy decisions, new config knobs (yaml) to describe sampling windows, splice thresholds, and quantization candidate lists, CLI flags to dry-run econ decisions, metrics/tracing hooks (span tags and unit-cost gauges), and end-to-end integration tests that simulate bursty Poisson + Pareto traffic. Rollout plan: feature is guarded behind feature flag `sample_splice_econ_adapter` and defaulted off. We will enable dry-run for 2 weeks in Canary region us-west-2 to collect econ deltas, then enable staged rollout (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with automatic rollback on cost regression >5% or p99 latency increase >10%. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for sample-splicing aggregation, kv-cache interactions, and edge-case empty-batch handling - [x] Integration test suite simulating burst profiles and validating p50/p95/p99 - [x] Econ model smoke tests with synthetic token-cost traces - [x] Documentation: config reference and runbook - [x] Observability: dashboards and alerts added - [x] Security review (no new secrets) Backwards compatibility: all runtime defaults unchanged until feature flag enabled. See linked Linear tasks for telemetry quotas and canary schedule (ENG-6241, PM-1912).

release_notes:
- Introduces sample-splicing micro-batcher (opt-in via feature flag) to improve GPU efficiency for microbursts
- Adds econ-adapter to auto-adjust quantization and prefill policies based on unit-econ signals (dry-run available)
- New observability: unit_econ_delta, unit_cost_mean, unit_cost_stddev, splice_window_ms
- Rollout guarded behind feature flag; no behavior change until enabled
notes_for_ops: If enabled in Canary: monitor metric 'unit_econ_delta' and 'api.p99_latency' dashboard. Default thresholds: rollback if unit_econ_delta > 0.05 for 10m or p99 latency increased by 10% for 5m. Use CLI flag --econ-dry-run to preview decisions. To disable immediately set feature flag sample_splice_econ_adapter=off and restart routing agent.
qa_steps: 1) Enable feature flag in staging; run integration-tests/burst_profiles/simulate_burst.yml 2) Verify p50/p95/p99 across routes unchanged, confirm unit_econ_delta reported as dry-run in telemetry 3) Toggle econ-adapter: allow quantization for low-risk routes and watch unit_cost_mean decrease 4) Force kv-cache pressure and confirm fallback to legacy batching occurs
